name: lodash-where-predicate-ignored-fasm
behavioral_change: From lodash v3.0.0, `_.where` always evaluates its second argument through `_.matches`, so only a source object for partial deep comparison is accepted. In v_old (2.4.2) `_.where` was literally `_.filter`, so a predicate function worked; in v_new (3.10.1) a function passed as the second argument yields a matcher that returns true for every element, and the whole collection is returned without any exception or deprecation notice.
downstream_effect: The downstream project's `AssetsFile.prototype.remove` uses `_.where` with a predicate function to drop entries matching a `canonicalLink` from `this.data.assets`; after the upgrade removal becomes a no-op and the array only grows. The two nodeunit failures ("AssertionError: 2 === 1" and "2 === 0") have frames only in test.js and nodeunit internals, and lodash, where, predicate, filter and matches never appear in the output.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in lib/assetsfile.js:63, replacing `_.where` with `_.filter` and leaving the anonymous predicate function unchanged.
documented_in: The lodash Changelog v3.0.0 section (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Changelog#v300) states "Ensured `_.findWhere` & `_.where` always use `_.matches`" (under Other Changes, not Compatibility Warnings); the API references at https://lodash.com/docs/2.4.2 and https://lodash.com/docs/3.10.1 show the parameter change from props to source, and the Deprecations page (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Deprecations) names `_.filter` as the replacement, with the 3.10.1 `_.filter` example code block showing the new code form.
failing_tests: test.js :: assets file methods (the two strictEqual assertions at lines 92 and 102 fail; nodeunit reports FAILURES: 2/14 assertions failed)
